brief.greeting: Good morning. Your inbox just got a few more LLM checklists and a kernel patch.

stories.headline: Scientific judgment still shaky
stories.body: **Benchmark reveals confidence gap:** The new SciResearch-Eval suite tests models on thermal‑property experiments; most report 95% confidence intervals that only contain the truth 20‑62% of the time. Shows calibration needs work.
stories.why: Miscalibrated confidence can mislead automated research pipelines.

stories.headline: New language unifies LLM workflows
stories.body: **Jac blends Python and agents:** The paper launches Agent‑Native Programming in Jac, a Python‑superset that lets you script LLM calls, state, and pipelines as first‑class constructs.
stories.why: Reduces glue code, making agentic apps easier to build and maintain.

stories.headline: Linux distro patch spree lands Monday
stories.body: **Multiple distros push fixes:** Debian, Fedora, Gentoo, Oracle, and SUSE released a batch of security updates covering dozens of packages, tightening the attack surface overnight.
stories.why: Keeps your servers and IoT devices from known exploits.

quick_hits.text: **Spanish LLM test:** Evaluates sentiment robustness on political posts with gold, ambiguous, synthetic subsets.

**Dograh voice AI:** Self‑hosted Speech‑to‑Speech platform with BYOK and telephony support.
**Revolut coding boost:** OpenAI models cut internal coding time by 30–60% while scaling fraud investigations.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow, and keep hacking.

highlights.title: Evaluating Cultural Reasoning and Robustness in LLMs for Spanish Political Discourse
highlights.summary: Evaluates LLM robustness for sentiment analysis of Spanish political social media using a diagnostic protocol with Gold, Ambiguous, and Synthetic subsets.
highlights.detail: The protocol combines three independent human annotation views to create reliable evaluation sets and adds a synthetic subset generated via model‑conditioned perplexity and counterfactual sentiment flips, targeting culturally situated affective cues.

highlights.title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents
highlights.summary: SciResearch-Eval benchmark measures scientific judgment on thermal‑property experiments, revealing calibration gaps where most models report 95% confidence intervals that contain the truth only 20‑62% of the time.
highlights.detail: The benchmark includes 9 models across 2,511 episodes, using a deliberately flawed simulator to test agents' ability to design experiments and report calibrated intervals. GPT‑6 Astra achieved 94% coverage, while Claude 5.5 performed poorly under default effort.

highlights.title: Algorithm Distillation for Safe In-Context Reinforcement Learning
highlights.summary: Revisits Safe Algorithm Distillation for in‑context RL, adding a two‑phase budget‑aware teacher to improve task discovery and cost management.
highlights.detail: Previous Safe AD showed zero or negative returns on locomotion benchmarks and rarely reached goals in CarGoal. The new approach separates exploration and exploitation phases, allowing more budget‑aware searching for hidden tasks before committing to safe actions.

related.title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks

highlights.title: Agent-Native by Design: A Programming Language for Agentic Applications
highlights.summary: The paper introduces Agent-Native Programming, realized in Jac, a Python-superset language that unifies LLM operations, workflow, and state handling.
highlights.detail: Jac adds typed model calls via "by llm()" and Object-Spatial Programming for workflow, aiming to reduce the split between application code and framework internals that hampers compiler optimizations.

related.title: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?

highlights.title: CompCert4Lean: Porting a Verified C Compiler to Lean in Six Weeks with Parallel Coding Agents
highlights.summary: CompCert4Lean ports the verified CompCert 3.17 C compiler from Coq to Lean in about six weeks using parallel LLM agents.
highlights.detail: The migration splits work by dependencies, audits translations, and reconstructs proofs in parallel, allowing the expert to focus on coordination; only three human interventions provided technical direction.

items.title: Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams
items.summary: OpenAI blog announces progress on computer‑use agents designed to assist healthcare teams.
items.detail: The post outlines goals for agents that can interact with software tools, retrieve patient data, and support clinical workflows, emphasizing safety, privacy, and integration with existing hospital systems.

items.title: Broadening access to AI for scientists
items.summary: OpenAI expands its ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program, granting free frontier‑model access to 200,000 scientists worldwide.
items.detail: The initiative aims to lower barriers for scientific inquiry by providing unrestricted usage of the latest language models, supporting tasks such as literature review, data analysis, and code generation.

related.title: Australian universities are creating AI-native graduates

items.title: How Revolut raises ambition without lowering the bar
items.summary: Revolut reports that using OpenAI models and Codex cuts its internal coding time by 30–60% while scaling financial‑crime investigations.
items.detail: The integration enables faster development of automation tools and maintains security standards, allowing the fintech firm to innovate without compromising compliance or data protection.

items.title: Model: chatrlabs/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-Omni-Quantized
items.summary: The Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-Omni-Quantized model for text-to-image has reached 142,901 downloads on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model is listed under the chatrlabs organization and is quantized for broader hardware compatibility. It targets uncensored generation, differentiating it from earlier Qwen variants. Popularity reflects strong community interest in open text-to-image tools.

items.title: Model: facebook/sam3
items.summary: Facebook's SAM3 mask-generation model has been downloaded 1,971,023 times on Hugging Face.
items.detail: SAM3 is part of the segment-anything family, focusing on generating segmentation masks from images. The high download count indicates wide adoption for computer‑vision pipelines. It is hosted under the facebook namespace.

items.title: Security updates for Monday
items.summary: Debian, Fedora, Gentoo, Oracle, and SUSE issued a batch of security updates for numerous packages on Monday.
items.detail: Updates cover components such as the Linux kernel, PostgreSQL 15, Firefox, MySQL 8.4/9.7, and various Rust libraries. Each distribution listed specific affected packages, reflecting coordinated vulnerability remediation across the Linux ecosystem.

items.title: [$] A new generation of futexes
items.summary: A new kernel patch series introduces a third futex class called "futex PING" for priority‑inheritance next‑generation mutexes.
items.detail: The proposal aims to reduce latency for contention‑heavy workloads by extending the existing two futex variants. It is authored by Suleiman Souhlal and targets users who find current futex performance insufficient.

items.title: A 3D Printed Pixel Clock, with a Twist
items.summary: Hackaday showcases a 3D‑printed pixel clock built with addressable RGB LED strips.
items.detail: The project leverages inexpensive LED strips to create a visual time‑display that can be customized via firmware. Its 3D‑printed housing demonstrates how rapid prototyping can simplify hardware hacking.

related.title: Print & Place: Add Embedded Electronics While FDM Printing

items.title: Binocular Chair Lets You Stargaze in Comfort
items.summary: A 3D‑printed chair integrates binoculars for comfortable stargazing.
items.detail: The design combines ergonomic seating with a mount that holds binoculars at eye level, reducing fatigue during long observation sessions. It exemplifies DIY approaches to enhancing amateur astronomy equipment.

items.title: Can’t Get the Right Cassette Mechanism? Have a Go at Making Your Own!
items.summary: Hackaday article notes that only one cassette tape deck mechanism is still in production, though the claim may be more nuanced.
items.detail: The piece explores the scarcity of new cassette mechanisms and hints at possible alternatives for enthusiasts seeking replacements or custom builds.

items.title: How Metal Foam Could Make Cars Safer
items.summary: Hackaday discusses metal foam as a material that could improve automotive crash safety by absorbing impact energy.
items.detail: The article outlines how the lightweight, porous structure of metal foam can dissipate forces, potentially allowing lighter car designs without sacrificing occupant protection.

items.title: Agent-Native by Design: A Programming Language for Agentic Applications
items.summary: The paper introduces Agent-Native Programming, realized in Jac, a Python-superset language that unifies LLM operations, workflow, and state handling.
items.detail: Jac adds typed model calls via "by llm()" and Object-Spatial Programming for workflow, aiming to reduce the split between application code and framework internals that hampers compiler optimizations.

related.title: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?

items.title: CompCert4Lean: Porting a Verified C Compiler to Lean in Six Weeks with Parallel Coding Agents
items.summary: CompCert4Lean ports the verified CompCert 3.17 C compiler from Coq to Lean in about six weeks using parallel LLM agents.
items.detail: The migration splits work by dependencies, audits translations, and reconstructs proofs in parallel, allowing the expert to focus on coordination; only three human interventions provided technical direction.

items.title: QuarkDB: A Hybrid Database System for Quantum Data Management
items.summary: QuarkDB is a hybrid database system designed to store and query both classical and quantum data, featuring a Quantum Structured Query Language.
items.detail: It combines a cost-based hybrid query engine, a three‑level intermediate representation for quantum execution, and a storage engine that handles versioned quantum datasets.

items.title: CIRT: Calculus of Inductive Refinement Types
items.summary: CIRT presents the first semantic model for refinement types supporting subtyping, SMT equality, impredicative polymorphism, and inductive types.
items.detail: The model uses partial equivalence relations over a Scott domain to prove consistency and to explain annotation‑independence, addressing prior inconsistencies in combined features.

items.title: Top-Level Operational Equilibrium: When is the response of a distributed system predictable from its own telemetry?
items.summary: The paper defines top-level operational equilibrium (TLOE) for distributed systems, requiring stationarity, a sufficient top-level aggregate, and time-reversibility, and proves the aggregate exists iff the minimal sufficient statistic of controls is time-reversible.
items.detail: TLOE links telemetry to predictability without adding new measurements, deriving the coarsest admissible aggregate rather than selecting one arbitrarily. The work formalizes conditions under which small control perturbations yield predictable responses, aiding operators in edge‑cloud adaptations.

items.title: Adaptive-Elbow Graph Traversal for Schema Retrieval in Text-to-SQL
items.summary: Adaptive-Elbow Graph Traversal (AEGT) is introduced as a property‑graph table retriever that dynamically selects schema slices for LLM‑based Text‑to‑SQL, improving over fixed‑budget embedding rankers.
items.detail: AEGT adjusts the number of tables per query and incorporates foreign‑key relationships, reducing noise and missed joins that hurt generation quality. It replaces static top‑k cosine similarity with a graph‑guided traversal, aiming for better recall without excessive cost.

items.title: dograh-hq/dograh
items.summary: dograh is an open‑source voice AI platform offering self‑hosted Speech‑to‑Speech, STT, and TTS with BYOK, visual workflow builder, MCP native and telephony support.
items.detail: Positioned as an on‑prem alternative to services like Vapi and Retell, dograh enables full data control and integration into existing telephony stacks, targeting teams needing customizable voice pipelines.

items.title: vstorm-co/agenticos
items.summary: agenticos is an open‑source, self‑hosted AI agent platform providing shared chat, RAG, skills, a real browser, and audit features, licensed under Apache‑2.0.
items.detail: The platform supports budget controls, approval workflows, and extensive monitoring, positioning itself as an enterprise‑grade alternative to ChatGPT Enterprise and Grok Bot while allowing use of private models.

items.title: BurntSushi/jiff
items.summary: jiff is a Rust datetime library designed to simplify correct time handling and encourage successful usage patterns.
items.detail: The library provides ergonomic APIs for parsing, formatting, and arithmetic on dates and times, aiming to reduce common pitfalls in Rust time manipulation.

items.title: HKUDS/RAG-Anything
items.summary: RAG-Anything is an all‑in‑one Retrieval‑Augmented Generation framework for Python.
items.detail: The project bundles components for document ingestion, indexing, and LLM‑driven generation, offering a unified interface for building RAG pipelines.

items.title: clice-io/clice
items.summary: clice-io/clice is a language server for C/C++, Objective‑C and CUDA built on Clang, featuring crash‑isolated workers, native C++20 module support, and a CLI for indexing, querying, and refactoring whole projects.
items.detail: The server runs each compilation task in a separate process to prevent crashes from affecting the whole IDE. It automatically discovers compilation contexts and supports modern C++20 module workflows without extra configuration. The CLI can operate on entire codebases, enabling batch refactoring and code navigation beyond typical editor integrations.

items.title: gabime/spdlog
items.summary: gabime/spdlog is a fast, header‑only C++ logging library offering low‑overhead logging with customizable sinks and formatting.
items.detail: spdlog achieves high performance by using compile‑time format strings and lock‑free queues where possible. It supports various output targets such as console, files, syslog, and rotating logs, and can be extended with user‑defined sinks. The library is widely adopted in performance‑critical applications due to its minimal runtime cost.
